Effective atmospheric emissivity

Source: R/metric-radiation.R
ef_atm_emissivity.Rd

Computes the effective broadband emissivity of a clear-sky atmosphere, \(\varepsilon_a\), from the clear-sky shortwave transmissivity. It is the emissivity used by ef_rl_in() for the incoming longwave radiation.

Usage

ef_atm_emissivity(tau_sw)

Arguments

tau_sw

Numeric. Total clear-sky broadband shortwave transmissivity on the horizontal \(\tau_{sw}\) [-], in the open interval (0, 1), normally ef_tau_sw_allen()$total (see Details).

Value

A numeric vector of \(\varepsilon_a\) [-] with the length and dim of tau_sw. Values above 1 (which occur only for \(\tau_{sw} < 0.0022776\)) are returned unchanged and are reported by the diagnostics of the stage (EF_RAD_ATM_EMISSIVITY_GT1).

Details

$$\varepsilon_a = 0.85 \left(-\ln \tau_{sw}\right)^{0.09}$$ The emissivity decreases as the transmissivity increases. The input must be the modelled clear-sky transmissivity, not an effective transmissivity derived from measured radiation, unless this is decided explicitly (decision RC-13): the empirical relation was proposed for clear skies.

tau_sw must be numeric and non-empty. Values outside (0, 1) (where the logarithm is undefined or the emissivity is zero) or infinite values raise earthflux_domain_error (also earthflux_input_error). Missing values propagate.

Verification status

CANDIDATA. Form and coefficients (0.85, 0.09) observed in the water package (v1.0), which attributes the form to Bastiaanssen (1995) and the coefficients to an internal report of Allen (2000); neither has been verified, nor its use in Allen et al. (2007), nor the range of transmissivities over which the coefficients were derived. Formulations in terms of vapour pressure and air temperature (e.g. Brutsaert) are an open alternative (decision RC-13).

References

Allen, R. G., Tasumi, M., & Trezza, R. (2007). Satellite-based energy balance for mapping evapotranspiration with internalized calibration (METRIC) - Model. Journal of Irrigation and Drainage Engineering, 133(4), 380-394. doi:10.1061/(ASCE)0733-9437(2007)133:4(380)

See also

Other radiation functions: ef_net_radiation(), ef_rl_in(), ef_rl_out(), ef_rs_in(), ef_solar_geometry(), ef_tau_sw()

Examples

ef_atm_emissivity(c(0.5, 0.7, 0.75, 0.9))
#> [1] 0.8224192 0.7746820 0.7598381 0.6941606
